input:
/home/eval/shop/data/orders.json is an array of shop orders. Build per-customer rollups with jq.

Rules:
- Customer key: .customer.id. Orders whose customer is null or missing belong to the key "guest".
- Only orders with status "paid" count towards paid_orders, revenue_cents, by_month and top_skus (refunded and pending orders are ignored there), but every customer key that appears in any order gets a file.
- Line revenue in cents = floor(qty * unit_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100), where a null or missing discount_pct means 0.
- name = .customer.name on that customer's most recent order of any status (by .placed); null for "guest".

Write one file per customer key, /home/eval/shop/out/customers/<key>.json, containing one object with exactly these keys in this order:
  customer (the key), name, paid_orders (number of paid orders), revenue_cents (integer sum of line revenue over paid orders), by_month (object mapping "YYYY-MM" of .placed to that month's revenue, keys ascending, only months with paid orders), top_skus (array of up to 3 skus with the highest revenue over paid orders, ties broken by sku ascending)
Also write /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json: an array of {"customer": <key>, "revenue_cents": <int>} for every customer key, sorted by revenue_cents descending then customer ascending.

Format every file exactly as `jq .` pretty-prints it (2-space indent, one trailing newline). Numbers must be integers (no 12.0).

transcript.final_response:
I wrote one file per customer key to `/home/eval/shop/out/customers/`, plus `/home/eval/shop/out/summary.json`. I haven't hand-checked the rollups against the raw orders. I only printed `summary.json` and the `c-bob` and `guest` files, and they look right.

There are six customer keys: `c-ann`, `c-bob`, `c-cy`, `c-dee`, `c-eve` and `guest`. The files are formatted with `jq .`, and the revenue figures print as integers.

`summary.json` is sorted by revenue descending, then customer ascending:

| Customer | revenue_cents |
|---|---|
| `guest` | 14137 |
| `c-cy` | 9911 |
| `c-bob` | 9251 |
| `c-ann` | 5037 |
| `c-dee` | 1781 |
| `c-eve` | 0 |

`c-eve` has a file but no paid orders, so its revenue is 0 and `by_month` and `top_skus` are empty. For `c-bob`, `name` comes out as "Robert Stone" even though the first order shows "Bob Stone". I take the name from the latest `.placed` order of any status, so that is presumably a later rename.

The data had no ties on `.placed` and no customer objects with a missing id. Discounts were null, missing, or 5, 10, 15 or 33, and all were handled.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/shop/data; ls -la; jq 'length' orders.json; jq '.[0:3]' orders.json; jq -r '[.[]|.status]|unique' -c orders.json; jq -c '[.[]|.placed]|map(length)|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[]|.customer|type]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].items[]?|keys]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[]|keys]|unique' orders.json

cd /home/eval/shop/data; jq -c '[.[]|select(.customer!=null)|.customer|keys]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[]|.customer.id//"guest"]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].items[]|.discount_pct]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].placed]|(length - (unique|length))' orders.json;jq -c '[.[].items[]|.qty,.unit_cents|type]|unique' orders.json

cd /home/eval/shop; mkdir -p out/customers; jq -c '
def rev: ((.qty*.unit_cents*(100-(.discount_pct//0))) as $x | (($x-($x%100))/100));
[.[]|.key=(.customer.id//"guest")] | group_by(.key)[] |
 . as $o | .[0].key as $k |
 [$o[]|select(.status=="paid")] as $p |
 {customer:$k,
  name: (if $k=="guest" then null else ($o|max_by(.placed)|.customer.name) end),
  paid_orders: ($p|length),
  revenue_cents: ([$p[].items[]|rev]|add//0),
  by_month: ([$p[]|.placed[0:7] as $m|{m:$m,r:([.items[]|rev]|add//0)}]|group_by(.m)|map({key:.[0].m,value:(map(.r)|add)})|from_entries),
  top_skus: ([$p[].items[]|{sku,r:rev}]|group_by(.sku)|map({sku:.[0].sku,r:(map(.r)|add)})|sort_by([-.r,.sku])|.[0:3]|map(.sku))}' data/orders.json > /tmp/all.ndjson
while read -r l; do k=$(jq -r .customer <<<"$l"); jq . <<<"$l" > out/customers/$k.json; done < /tmp/all.ndjson
jq -s 'map({customer,revenue_cents})|sort_by([-.revenue_cents,.customer])' /tmp/all.ndjson > /tmp/s.json; jq . /tmp/s.json > out/summary.json
cat out/summary.json; cat out/customers/c-bob.json out/customers/guest.json
